name: users
description: Target schema for gradido2 (PostgreSQL/SQLite), derived from the legacy MariaDB table.

columns.name: remote
columns.description: A member of another community, known here only by reference.

columns.name: gradido_id
columns.description: Stable public identifier. Legacy stores it as char(36); gradido2 uses a uuid column.

columns.name: community_id
columns.description: The community this member belongs to, by row id.
columns.note: DO NOT CHANGE THIS BACK TO A UUID. Legacy carries users.community_uuid, a char(36) with a foreign key on communities.community_uuid, and gradido2 deliberately does not: a uuid is 16 bytes of key in every row, every index entry and every join, to identify a set that has a handful of members. The uuid stays the community's public, federation-facing identity and lives in communities.community_uuid alone; inside this database a community is its row id. The same change is intended for the other tables that still name community_uuid here — each one still has to be checked, so a disagreement between this file and transactions.json is work not yet done, not a mistake to reconcile in this direction.

columns.name: email_id
columns.description: The contact row holding the login and contact email.

columns.name: password
columns.description: LEGACY_SHORTHASH result: SipHash-2-4 of an argon2id key, 8 bytes. 0 means no password.
columns.open: Verify only, never write. Rows still using it are migrated on their next successful login. The column may be dropped once password_encryption_type has no EMAIL or GRADIDO_ID rows left.

columns.name: password_hash
columns.description: argon2id in PHC string format, parameters and salt included. Set when password_encryption_type is ARGON2ID_PHC.

columns.name: avatar_visible_to_members
columns.description: Whether other members may see this member's picture. About who may look, not about a foreign system.

columns.name: location
columns.open: Legacy uses a MariaDB geometry column with a custom transformer. PostgreSQL would use PostGIS or two numeric columns; SQLite has neither. Decide before the first user-facing feature needs it — this is the one column with no neutral type.

columns.name: deleted_at
columns.description: Soft delete. Every query on this table must exclude non-null unless it deliberately includes deleted rows.

notes: The uniqueness of gradido_id is per community, not global — migration 0073 replaced the single-column unique when foreign users were introduced. An implementation that assumes a global unique gradido_id is wrong.

The community is referenced by row id, not by uuid — see the note on community_id, and do not "correct" it towards legacy. gradido_id is still a uuid: that one is this member's public identity and leaves the database, which is exactly the distinction the two columns make.
created_at, deleted_at and gms_registered_at are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. deleted_at null means not deleted — never 0.

Identifiers are uint64 throughout. Legacy is inconsistent here — users.id is int unsigned while referrer_id, contribution_link_id and publisher_id, which point at it, are bigint unsigned. A foreign key narrower than its target truncates silently in C, so gradido2 uses one width everywhere.
A user has at most one password representation: password (legacy) or password_hash (current), selected by password_encryption_type.
